LESSON: READING 12.2.1 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Reading 12.2.1 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 12.2.1 Comprehension, part of Strand 12 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can we tell where events have taken place in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 12.2.1 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak engagingly is enhanced as they retell the story in their own words.

• Learning to learn: The learner’s ability to learn independently is developed as they are motivated to read a variety of texts for information.

Values:
• Unity: Cooperation is cultivated as the learner collaborates with others in group activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is nurtured as their reading comprehension skills improves.

Link to other Learning Areas;

The learner applies comprehension skills when reading texts in Kiswahili and Indigenous Languages.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

• Braille books

• Digital devices with assistive technology,
